back: Permissions saying which tables, queries, forms or reports a user may use and whether they may read only or also add, change and delete.
A saved query given to users instead of the table, so they see only selected fields and records.
An automatic log of who accessed or changed data, what changed (old and new values) and when.
Each user gets only the access rights needed for their job.
Full: copies everything. Incremental: copies only changes since the last backup. Restore = last full + every incremental since, in order.
A fire, flood or theft could destroy the server and any copy kept beside it.

front: Encryption at rest and in transit
back: At rest: the stored database file is scrambled. In transit: data is scrambled as it travels over a network.
Store them hashed (one-way scrambled), never as plain text, so a stolen table does not reveal them.
A password checks who the user is; access rights decide what that user may do.
